rules.statement: In a Helm chart, gate an optional feature section that stands for operator consent behind an explicit boolean `enabled` value defaulting to `false`, not behind whether some other value such as a location or identity is set.
rules.why: Every chart value has a default, so a value's presence can't stand for an absent section. A location or identity used as the switch would re-register a vendor the operator turned off, and would leave no way to enable a mode that has no location.
rules.check: Look for chart templates that render a configuration section only when a non-boolean value like a region, URI or identity is non-empty, where that section's existence changes behavior on its own.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, fail the render for a value that has no effect on its own, such as a location set on a feature that isn't enabled, or a credential configuration that is only half set.
rules.why: The chart refuses any release the host would refuse, and a setting that silently does nothing hides a misconfiguration.
rules.check: When a diff adds dependent chart values, check that the templates `fail` if the dependent value is set while its feature is disabled, or if only some fields of a multi-field identity are set.

rules.statement: In chart values, model a collection of entries identified by an id as a map keyed by that id, not as a list of objects with an id field.
rules.why: A map can't name one id twice, and a list can.
rules.check: Look for new list-valued chart values whose items carry an `id`/`kid`/`name` field that must be unique.

rules.statement: When two chart components render the same credential or configuration shape, render it with one shared helper that takes a parameter dict, and define the shape once in the shared schema `definitions`, rather than copying the helper or the schema.
rules.why: Two renderings of one shape drift.
rules.check: Look for duplicated template helpers or duplicated values-schema objects that render or validate the same structure for different components.

rules.statement: Give each deployed component its own workload identity and mount a cloud vendor's credentials only into the pods of a component that uses that vendor; never reuse a more privileged component's identity.
rules.why: Least privilege: the server's identity creates and destroys keys and its federated credentials trust the server's ServiceAccount, so another component reusing it would get powers it doesn't need.
rules.check: Look for chart templates that mount one component's vendor credentials or ServiceAccount into another component's pods, or that mount them without a condition on that component using the vendor.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, don't recommend `extraEnv` or other raw passthrough values for settings the chart models directly.
rules.why: Passthrough bypasses the chart's refusals and its credential mounts.
rules.check: Look for docs, CI values or templates that set modeled configuration through `extraEnv` instead of the dedicated chart values.

rules.statement: Restrict user-supplied identifiers that become part of .NET configuration keys or environment variable names to a safe pattern, such as letters and digits separated by single `.`, `_` or `-`, with a length limit, and refuse ids that are equal when compared without case.
rules.why: An id containing `__` would split into separate configuration sections, the id must be a valid environment variable name, and .NET configuration keys are case-insensitive, so two ids that differ only in case collide.
rules.check: Look for values or inputs that are interpolated into `Section__<id>__*` env names or configuration paths without pattern validation or a case-insensitive uniqueness check.
